title: Reface review: face swap, Unboring pricing and alternatives
summary: Reface review covering its mobile app, Unboring web workflow, face-swap pricing, retention, limitations, and current alternatives.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Reface is worth considering for template-led mobile face swaps and short entertainment clips. Its clearest strength is established mobile app plus unboring web face swap and animation. The main limitation is web and mobile products, limits and billing paths differ. Magic Hour is the stronger fit when you want image, GIF and video face swap inside a broader image, video and audio workspace.**


This vendor-authored review was checked against[Reface official product and policy pages](https://reface.ai/reface/) on September 20, 2026. Magic Hour publishes this guide and is included as an alternative. It is a documentation review, not a retained cross-tool quality benchmark.


## What is Reface?


Reface is an AI face-swap product for replacing a face in an image or video. Established mobile app plus Unboring web face swap and animation. Use only media you own or have permission to edit, and obtain explicit consent from every identifiable person.


## What Reface does well


Template-led mobile face swaps and short entertainment clips. Its workflow removes much of the manual masking and compositing required by conventional editing. That convenience does not prove every output is accurate: inspect eyes, teeth, hairlines, skin edges, occlusion, lighting and identity across the full clip.


## Reface pricing and access


Reface’s Unboring web page currently lists Basic from $7.58 per month billed annually and Premium from $9.99 per month billed annually. It lists a 15-second maximum for web face-swap video. App Store pricing and mobile features can differ, so verify the exact Reface surface you intend to use.


## Privacy, consent and commercial use


Reface’s how-it-works page says original photos used for face swap are removed from its cloud within 48 hours plus a short server-operations period, and face embeddings are completely erased by day four. Generated avatar assets follow different retention rules, so do not generalize one workflow’s policy to another.


A commercial-use label does not clear publicity, copyright, trademark or contractual rights. Keep written consent, source licenses and disclosure records. Never use face swap to impersonate, deceive, harass or create intimate imagery without consent.

## How to test Reface fairly


Use one permitted portrait, one difficult side angle and one short motion clip. Keep resolution, duration and source files constant. Record attempts, processing time, charged credits, watermarks, export resolution and whether the output was usable without manual repair.


Reject outputs with identity drift, unstable jaw or hair boundaries, flicker, incorrect occlusion, changed expression, altered skin tone or artifacts around glasses and hands. Compare cost per accepted output rather than cost per generation.


## Verdict


Reface has a defensible place for template-led mobile face swaps and short entertainment clips. Web and mobile products, limits and billing paths differ. Test one representative job and verify current policies before committing sensitive media or recurring production.
